solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Minister’s measure of spin

definitions.note: read as a possessive: the Rev's

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to a clergyman, whose title is abbreviated Rev
second meaning: revolutions per minute of an engine

explanation.surface: A government minister's talent for spin being gauged, as if spin-doctoring could be measured.
explanation.walkthrough: The minister is a clergyman, not a politician, and the spin is mechanical rotation rather than media manipulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Engine speed is counted in revolutions, colloquially shortened, while a clergyman's written title is the same abbreviation plus possessive.

clue.text: Some toast the good times, in reviews

blocks.note: a round of toast is a slice or batch of it
ups, as in ups and downs

explanation.surface: Critics raising a glass to happier days within their reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like a drink to celebration, but here it is bread: a round of toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A news round-up is a summary of recent events, the same job as a review of the week.

clue.text: Wagon train official in front

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for a noun; think 'in the vanguard'

blocks.note: a van is a railway wagon
the guard is the official in charge of a train

explanation.surface: A wagon train of pioneers with its official riding at the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wagon train' reads as one Wild West phrase, but it splits: wagon is one piece, train official the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard is the leading division of an advancing army or movement, so being there means being foremost.

clue.text: Mutant has ten arms: that spells trouble!

indicators.note: a mutant is a changed version of its original form, so the letters that follow are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A ten-armed mutant monster heralds disaster, like a line from a B-movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutant' seems to be the subject, but it only tells you to change the letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassment is persistent pestering or bothering, a kind of trouble inflicted on someone.

clue.text: Do books sound mostly tedious at first?

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped
at first points to the opening letter only of the word it follows

blocks.note: audio means sound; lose its last letter
the opening letter of tedious

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether books seem boring at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do books' is accountancy jargon: to do the books is to check the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is the formal inspection of a company's financial accounts, so to perform one is to examine them.

clue.text: Unaccompanied neighbour of C and R White, female

blocks.clueFragment: neighbour of C and R White
blocks.note: in the cartoon strip, Andy Capp lives next to Chalkie and Ruby White
Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An unaccompanied woman living beside a couple called White.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Capp is a long-running British newspaper cartoon about a work-shy northerner; his mate Chalkie White and wife Ruby live nearby, so the neighbour is A. Capp.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappella singing is performed by voices alone, without any instrumental accompaniment.

clue.text: Small boy upset about groups of Santa’s helpers being collected

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards
about means around, so the outer pieces surround the middle

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
elves help Santa, and posses are gangs of them
Des is short for Desmond

explanation.surface: A little lad in tears about the gathering of Christmas elves.
explanation.walkthrough: S and the reversed boy's name wrap around the elf posses; the whole answer reads S, ELF POSSES, SED.
explanation.definitionFit: Collected here means calm and composed, which is exactly what a self-possessed person is.

clue.text: Was green jockey going through finish?

indicators.note: to go through something is to pass inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: to jockey for position is to vie
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Was the inexperienced jockey still riding as he crossed the finish line?
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'green' and 'jockey' want to be racing words; green is envy and jockey is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Green with envy is the idiom, so being green means feeling jealous of someone.

clue.text: Blast experienced after impact, just shells going up

indicators.note: a shell is the outside casing, so only the outer letters of each word stay
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the order flips

blocks.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: An explosion felt after artillery hits, with shells rising into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The military picture of shells and blasts hides a selection device: 'shells' are the outer letters of three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast in the sense of a furious verbal attack, a rant or harangue, is a tirade.

clue.text: Component in modem annually put back without label

indicators.note: a component is a part inside a whole, so the answer is a run of letters within the words
put back means moved backwards, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A part inside a modem gets relabelled once a year, sounding like routine IT maintenance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the end of modem and the start of annually, and read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a label has no name attached, so it has not been identified by any title.

clue.text: Social inadequacy of youth not allowing females to board coaster

indicators.note: to board a vehicle is to get inside it, so these pieces go within another

blocks.note: a lad is a young man
no women allowed means just men
a coaster is a mat for a drink

explanation.surface: A socially awkward teenager at a men-only rollercoaster, keeping girls off the ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaster' looks like a fairground ride or a ship, but it is the mat under your drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladjustment is a failure to cope with ordinary social surroundings, which is a kind of social inadequacy.

clue.text: Total fan of Chicago gangster

blocks.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster
a fan is a lover of something

explanation.surface: Someone who is a complete devotee of a notorious Chicago mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the fan as belonging to Al: an Al lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-over pattern covers everything, so it means complete or total in extent.

clue.text: Forty on board a single flight assisted?

blocks.clueFragment: Forty on board a single flight
blocks.note: surface reading: forty passengers aboard one aeroplane flight
setter's reading: on a dartboard, one dart, the thing with a flight, can score forty by hitting the doubled twenty segment at the top

explanation.surface: Forty passengers aboard one flight, perhaps with assisted boarding.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a dartboard and a flight is the finned tail of a dart, so this is one dart's best double.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty sector sits at the top of a dartboard, and hitting its double ring scores twice twenty, forty points.

clue.text: At hearing, prosecuted for fraud

indicators.note: at a hearing things are heard, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to be taken to court is to be sued; the P is silent

explanation.surface: Someone taken to court at a hearing on fraud charges.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom 'hearing' is the sound signal; a pseud is a pretentious poseur, a British colloquialism.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseud pretends to learning or taste they lack, so they are a fake or impostor.

clue.text: Adlestrop is a fantastic work of poetry

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful and unreal, so these letters take on an imagined new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Praising Adlestrop, Edward Thomas's short poem about a train halting at a Gloucestershire station.
explanation.walkthrough: Adlestrop really is a poem, so it looks like the definition; it is only the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's Paradise Lost is the great English epic poem about the Fall of Man.

clue.text: Maybe eleven things left by singers, or two left by barbers?

blocks.note: a cricket or football team of eleven is a side
a singer here is something that singes, and it leaves burns

explanation.surface: What choirs leave behind compared with what hairdressers leave behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singers' are not vocalists but things that singe.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are the strips of hair down each cheek that a barber leaves when trimming, one on either side.

clue.text: To walk, it needs varying amount of power

indicators.note: varying means changing, so these letters change their order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Walking takes differing amounts of energy, like a note on exercise physiology.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the surface sentence but the letters run straight across it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilowatt is a thousand watts, a standard unit measuring electrical power.

clue.text: Spotted flyer, one badly torn, on road

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A spotted poster, one of them badly torn, stuck up on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like a leaflet, especially next to 'torn', but it is something that flies. Ladybird is the British name for the ladybug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybird is a small red beetle with black spots that flies, hence a spotted flyer.

clue.text: Fast Sunday bike rider’s frenzy? I’m gripped by it!

indicators.note: to be gripped by something is to be held inside it

blocks.note: a quad bike
rage is a frenzy, as in road rage
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
taken as written

explanation.surface: A speed-crazed biker's Sunday fury, told in the first person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is not speed but abstaining from food: Quadragesima is the first Sunday of Lent. 'It' as sex appeal is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Quadragesima, from Latin for fortieth, names the first Sunday in Lent, the forty-day season of fasting.

clue.text: Letter for one young Suffolk lawyer

blocks.note: a Suffolk is a breed of sheep, and its young is a lamb
a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A letter written for a junior solicitor practising in Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk is an English county, but here it is the sheep breed named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh character of the Greek alphabet, the equivalent of our L.

clue.text: Outlaw and doctor have united in jail

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to outlaw is to ban
a general practitioner
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: An outlaw and a doctor who have joined forces behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' reads as a bandit but is a verb, to ban; bang up is British slang for locking someone in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: To bang someone up is informal British usage for imprisoning them, putting them in a cell.

clue.text: Stop when all at sea, maybe, with a Jumbo

definitions.text: Stop when all at sea, maybe

blocks.note: taken as written
jumbo means huge, vast

explanation.surface: Halting a confused elephant, or a jumbo jet in trouble over the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All at sea' usually means confused; here it is literal, on board ship, where the sailor's cry for stop is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is the old nautical command telling sailors to cease or hold what they are doing.

clue.text: Helps to track earlier episodes

blocks.note: to back someone is to help them
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Tips for following up on previous instalments of a TV series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' looks like a verb meaning follow; it is a railway, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstory is the history of events that happened to characters before the narrative begins.

clue.text: Cold fish, one potted, one smoked

indicators.note: something potted is placed in a pot, so this piece goes inside the others

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the Roman numeral for one
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A deli counter of fish: one cold, one potted, one smoked.
explanation.walkthrough: The list suggests three fish preparations, but 'one smoked' is the definition and potted is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is a roll of tobacco leaves that is lit and smoked, making it a thing one smokes.

clue.text: Worry, having hold on spy

blocks.note: to bug is to spy with a hidden microphone
to bear is to hold or carry

explanation.surface: Anxiety about being in the grip of a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means placed after, so the hold piece follows the spy piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of annoyance or dread, something that nags at a person.

clue.text: Reflected whether to include a grand old colonel

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the order runs backwards

blocks.note: if can mean whether
to add is to include
taken as written
G stands for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Pondering whether to bring an aged, distinguished colonel along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflected' looks like it means pondered, but it reverses everything that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Muammar Gaddafi, the Libyan dictator killed in 2011, always styled himself Colonel.

clue.text: Exotic striptease, papa having replaced tango for starters!

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters are made unfamiliar
replacing means swapping one thing out for another
for here means in place of, marking which letter is swapped out

blocks.note: taken as written
papa is P in the NATO alphabet
tango is T in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An exotic striptease laid on as the warm-up act of an evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap one T of striptease for P, then rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetisers and starters are both British terms for the small dishes served before the main course of a meal.

clue.text: Boss’s report incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete means lacking its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a study is a written report of research, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A manager's report left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not a manager but a raised ornamental knob, and the apostrophe-s is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round projecting knob or stud, as on a shield or ceiling.
